aspect: The injury is compounded by the response to it
description: Rejection by spouse or family, unmarriageability, removal from the household. The social consequence is frequently more destructive than the assault, and is entirely a decision made by the victim's own people.
energy_note: Attacked twice, the second time at home.

description: Since the consequence of telling is often exile from the family, non-disclosure is a correct strategy. Which means prevalence is systematically understated in every dataset, including this one.
energy_note: A number nobody has, on purpose.

aspect: Children born of it occupy an impossible position
description: Identified with the attacker, raised by the attacked, belonging to neither, and often without legal status or documented parentage.

aspect: Men are victims too, and are documented almost nowhere
description: Sexual violence against men in detention is a recognised and systematically under-reported instrument. Disclosure rates are lower still, and services essentially do not exist.
energy_note: A category of victim with no services at all.
notes: Deliberately included: the male-specific material in assets/text/iran does not cover this and it belongs somewhere.

aspect: SECONDARY - it removes the family as a support structure
description: The single most protective factor after war trauma is family support. This injury specifically destroys it, which is why the outcomes are so much worse.
energy_note: The one injury that takes the cure with it.
